item.title: Josh Naylor's Surprising Slow Start: Why the Mariners Shouldn't Panic Yet
item.description:
A .104 batting average from your $92.5 million offseason centerpiece is enough to make any fanbase reach for the panic button. But what if the numbers hiding beneath that ugly surface tell a completely different story?

That is exactly the situation unfolding with Josh Naylor and the Seattle Mariners in the early weeks of the 2026 MLB season. And on April 13, Naylor may have fired the first shot of a turnaround, launching a homer against the Houston Astros that scored Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez in a much-needed offensive burst.

item.title: Rays Surge Forward: Yankees Sweep, New Ownership, and a Stadium Shaping Tampa's Future
item.description:
The Tampa Bay Rays just swept the New York Yankees — and that might not even be the biggest story surrounding the franchise right now.

Between a buzzing on-field product, a new billion-dollar ownership group settling in, and a proposed ballpark that could reshape downtown Tampa, the Rays are at a crossroads that will define the franchise for decades. Here is everything you need to know.

Key Takeaways

  • The Rays completed a three-game sweep of the Yankees with a walk-off 5-4 extra-inning win on April 12.
  • Pitcher Joe Boyle was placed on the 15-day injured list with a right elbow strain — no structural damage found.
  • New owner Patrick Zalupski closed on the team for an estimated $1.7 billion in late 2025.
  • The Rays revealed a timeline and funding plan for a proposed new ballpark, though Tampa leaders stress the deal is not yet final.

Rays Dominate Yankees in Three-Game Sweep

The Rays capped a statement weekend at Tropicana Field by hanging on for a 5-4 victory over the Yankees on Sunday, April 12, completing the three-game sweep and extending New York’s losing streak to four games.

item.title: Ryan McMahon's Alarming Slump: What's Next for the Yankees Third Baseman?
item.description:
When the New York Yankees traded for Ryan McMahon at the 2025 deadline, they believed they were locking down elite defense at third base for years to come. Barely into the 2026 season, McMahon is hitting .087 slugging through his first 23 at-bats — and the conversation has already shifted from swing fixes to potential replacements.

Key Takeaways

  • McMahon is 2-for-23 with 11 strikeouts to start 2026, a 40% whiff rate far above his 32.3% career mark
  • Top prospect George Lombard Jr. could be called up before the All-Star break, per MLB insider Jim Bowden
  • The Yankees may also explore trades involving outfield prospects Jasson Dominguez or Spencer Jones
  • McMahon is in the fifth year of a six-year, $70 million contract

Ryan McMahon’s Early-Season Numbers Paint a Grim Picture

The Yankees acquired McMahon from the Colorado Rockies last July, sending pitching prospects Griffin Herring and Josh Grosz the other way. At the time, McMahon was a National League All-Star and ranked in the 91st percentile with 4 outs above average at the hot corner — a legitimate Gold Glove-caliber defender.

item.title: Dbacks vs Mets: Mauricio's Walk-Off Caps Thrilling Extra-Inning Battle at Citi Field
item.description:
Dbacks vs Mets: Mauricio’s Walk-Off Caps Thrilling Extra-Inning Battle at Citi Field

What happens when a rookie gets called up to replace one of baseball’s biggest stars and delivers in his very first at-bat? That’s exactly the scene that unfolded at Citi Field on Tuesday, April 7, as the Mets edged the Diamondbacks 4-3 in 10 innings on a frigid, wind-whipped afternoon in New York.

Key Takeaways

  • Ronny Mauricio delivered a pinch-hit walk-off RBI single in his first at-bat after being called up to replace the injured Juan Soto.
  • The Mets extended their win streak to four games, improving to 7-4 on the season.
  • Extreme wind at Citi Field caused a Brooks Raley sweeper to move 35 inches horizontally — nearly double its usual break.
  • Start times for the series were shifted to 4 p.m. ET due to brutal cold conditions.
  • Merrill Kelly is set to throw 85 pitches in extended spring training on April 9 as part of his comeback.

Mauricio Makes an Instant Impact

Ronny Mauricio didn’t need a warm-up. Called up to fill the roster spot left by an injured Juan Soto, the young infielder stepped to the plate as a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the 10th inning and laced a walk-off RBI single to clinch the victory.

item.title: Pittsburgh Pirates Surge Into 2026: Griffin's Debut, Skenes' Dominance, and a Franchise Reborn
item.description:
All eyes in baseball are on Pittsburgh. For the first time in what feels like an eternity, it’s for a positive reason.

The Pittsburgh Pirates have called up the unanimous No. 1 prospect in all of baseball — shortstop Konnor Griffin — for their 2026 home opener at PNC Park against the Baltimore Orioles. Combined with a revamped roster, a Cy Young ace, and a front office that finally opened the checkbook, this franchise looks fundamentally different from the team that limped to a 71-91 record just one year ago.

item.title: Corbin Carroll's Stunning Comeback: How the D-backs Star Defied a Broken Hand
item.description:
Most players who break a bone in their hand seven weeks before Opening Day accept they’ll start the season on the injured list. Corbin Carroll is not most players.

The Arizona Diamondbacks superstar not only made it back for Opening Day — he announced his return with a 107.8 MPH, 403-foot home run off Justin Verlander, proving that a broken hamate bone couldn’t slow him down.

Key Takeaways

  • Carroll broke his right hamate bone on Feb. 10, had surgery Feb. 11, and was back for Opening Day on March 26
  • In his home opener on March 30, he went 2-for-4 with a triple, a homer, 4 RBI, and exit velocities over 107 MPH
  • He became only the third left-handed batter to homer off Tarik Skubal since 2024
  • Carroll is coming off a career-best 30-30 season in 2025 when he led MLB with 17 triples

Corbin Carroll’s Hamate Bone Injury and Rapid Recovery

On February 10, during a live batting-practice session at Salt River Fields, Carroll felt something snap. He told Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo he thought he’d broken his hand. He wasn’t kidding.

item.title: Max Fried Dominates as Yankees Ace — Opening Week Brilliance Signals a Historic Season
item.description:
Has any pitcher made a louder first impression with a new team this season? Max Fried answered that question emphatically on Opening Night, delivering a shutout gem that set the tone for what could be a historic Yankees campaign.

Key Takeaways

  • Max Fried pitched a dominant shutout in the Yankees’ Opening Night victory over the San Francisco Giants on March 26, 2026
  • The Yankees swept the Giants in their opening series, with Fried accomplishing a historic feat during the sweep
  • Fried’s brilliance carried the Yankees even as Aaron Judge went hitless in the opener
  • His next marquee matchup: facing Logan Gilbert and the Seattle Mariners on April 1

Max Fried’s Opening Night Masterclass Sets the Standard

When the Yankees took the field on March 25 for Opening Night against the San Francisco Giants, all eyes were on their prized offseason acquisition. Max Fried didn’t just meet expectations — he shattered them.

item.title: Sal Stewart's Stunning Transformation Has the Reds Dreaming Big for 2026
item.description:
A 22-year-old drops 26 pounds in one offseason, mashes his way through spring training with a 1.066 OPS, and earns the cleanup spot on Opening Day — that’s the Sal Stewart story heading into 2026, and Cincinnati hasn’t been this excited about a young hitter in years.

Key Takeaways

  • Sal Stewart lost 26 pounds this offseason to prepare for his first full MLB season
  • He slashed an impressive 1.066 OPS with 3 home runs and 4 stolen bases in Cactus League play
  • Manager Terry Francona has slotted him into the cleanup spot on Opening Day
  • Stewart is ranked as baseball’s No. 22 overall prospect and Cincinnati’s top prospect
  • His 2025 debut produced 5 home runs in just 58 plate appearances

Sal Stewart’s 26-Pound Offseason Overhaul

Body transformations in baseball aren’t new. But the intent behind Stewart’s matters.
